1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet.js – this is the React implementation of CodeSnippet and needs to accept a new disabled prop, apply a disabled CSS class, suppress focus/tabIndex, and prevent clicks on CopyButton and expand.  
2. packages/components/src/components/code-snippet/code-snippet.js – this is the vanilla JS/web-component version; it likewise must recognize a disabled attribute, add a disabled class, and block user interactions.  
3. packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet-story.js – the Storybook story must be updated to include knobs/controls for the disabled state so designers and developers can preview and test the new behavior.  
4. packages/components/src/components/code-snippet/code-snippet.config.js – the configuration for the vanilla component variants should include a disabled example so the static HTML demos reflect the new disabled styling and usage guidance.
1.bug_scenario: The two screenshots illustrate the need for a “disabled” state on the CodeSnippet component. In the first image, the snippet is being used as a placeholder for the webhook URL (“Loading…”) and shows the copy button and is keyboard-focusable even though no value is yet available. In the second image, other fields and buttons are properly greyed-out and non-focusable when disabled, but the CodeSnippet remains fully active. The request is to add a disabled prop to CodeSnippet so that it renders with a greyed-out style, removes keyboard focus, and disables any copy or expand interactions until a real value is present.
